name: Fleets and Admirals: Sea Power from Salamis to Midway
description: Oared galleys, treasure ships, wooden walls and carrier fleets: the navies and commanders whose battles decided who ruled the waves.

checkpoints.name: Oars and rams
checkpoints.note: At Salamis in 480 BCE Greek ships beat a larger Persian fleet in narrow waters. The Delian League, led by Athens, made a fleet the base of Athenian power. In 31 BCE the sea battle of Actium decided the last of Rome's civil wars.

checkpoints.name: Longships and dhows
checkpoints.note: Viking longships raided and traded from the 790s, Byzantine ships used Greek fire to defend Constantinople, and Arab and Indian Ocean sailors crossed the monsoon seas in dhows. For more than a thousand years sea power belonged to many peoples beyond the Mediterranean.

checkpoints.name: Galleys, junks and galleons
checkpoints.note: Zheng He's treasure voyages sent Ming fleets across the Indian Ocean from 1405. The Mary Rose sank in 1545, the Royal Navy grew under the Tudors, and Francis Drake and storms helped defeat the Spanish Armada in 1588. At Lepanto in 1571 a Christian galley alliance beat the Ottomans, and in the 1590s Admiral Yi Sun-sin's turtle ships stopped a Japanese invasion of Korea.

checkpoints.name: Wooden walls
checkpoints.note: HMS Victory, launched in 1765, was Horatio Nelson's flagship at Trafalgar in 1805, where the British fleet beat French and Spanish ships and Nelson was killed. The US frigate USS Constitution, launched in 1797, showed that a young navy could fight.

checkpoints.name: Steel and carriers
checkpoints.note: HMS Dreadnought of 1906 set the pattern for modern battleships, and in 1905 Japan destroyed a Russian fleet at Tsushima. At Jutland in 1916 the British and German battle fleets met in the largest sea battle of World War I. In World War II the Bismarck was sunk in 1941, Yamamoto planned the attack on Pearl Harbor, Nimitz's carriers won at Midway in 1942, and the giant Yamato was sunk in 1945.
